deviation_mechanism: The optimization treats each layer thickness as an independent continuous variable. Broadband chirped reflectors rely on a cumulative, coherent phase shift across interfaces to gradually tune the effective optical path length and extend high-reflectance bandwidth. Without an explicit chirp-enforcing constraint or functional parametrization (e.g., polynomial thickness gradient), the solver minimizes the local Fresnel reflection error layer-by-layer. Adjacent layers therefore compensate each other's optical impedance mismatches independently rather than cooperatively building the global index/thickness gradient required for chirp. This decouples local interference tuning from the global spectral shaping mechanism, driving the system into quasi-random local minima that scatter the thickness profile instead of forming a monotonic trend.
